citations: xds/internal/balancer/priority/balancer.go:222-233 (Close holds b.mu via defer across the whole body, including the child.stop() loop, with a comment stating this stops init timers)
xds/internal/balancer/priority/balancer_child.go:143-163 (startInitTimer/AfterFunc takes cb.parent.mu with defer Unlock and checks timerW.stopped)
balancer/balancer.go:368-370 (UpdateClientConnState/Close guaranteed synchronous from one goroutine)
items.basis: Close() acquires b.mu with defer Unlock() at the very top of its body and only releases it after iterating every child and calling stop(), which calls stopInitTimer() synchronously (setting timerW.stopped=true and calling timer.Stop()) while still holding the same lock; the code's own comment at balancer.go:227-228 states this loop exists specifically to stop the init timers. run()'s vulnerable early-return branch can only be taken once b.done.HasFired() is true, and that flag is only set inside Close() while Close() already holds b.mu, so run()'s Lock() call cannot even proceed until Close() has released the lock via its defer — by which point every existing child's timer has already been neutralized under that same lock. Any AfterFunc that races Close() either finishes via its own defer Unlock() before Close() begins, or blocks on ordinary bounded contention until Close()'s defer fires and then observes timerW.stopped==true and returns immediately. In every possible interleaving the timer goroutine is never permanently blocked by the pre-fix leak, so the 'second waiter class' claim is refuted, not merely unconfirmed.
